title: One finger across the strings
summary: Use a barre to replace open strings.

steps.title: One finger across the strings
steps.body:
**barre** means pressing more than one string at the same fret with one finger. For this F major shape, lay your fretting-hand index finger across strings 6 through 1 at fret 1. Add fret 3 on strings 5 and 4, and fret 2 on string 3.

**Why it matters:** The finger across the neck replaces open strings, so a full chord shape can move to another fret.

steps.title: Read the positions
steps.body: The thick band means one finger spans fret 1. The other dots sit at frets 3, 3 and 2. The sounds are F, C, F, A, C and F: the three names F, A and C make F major. All six strings are played.

items.prompt: Play F, A and C together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Make it comfortable
steps.body: On your guitar, first try only strings 2 and 1 at fret 1 with one finger. Add the rest gradually. Keep your wrist comfortable, use only enough pressure for a clear sound, and stop if it hurts. Tap the positions for the app check; it checks sounds, not which finger you used.
